scope: Known pinned SDK save-path budget and explicit private native-work storage. This record does not establish successful native save, launch or navigation.

implementation.pathBudget: Known document-check UUID and NativeSaved archive expansion into .SC2Map.temp/enUS.SC2Data/LocalizedData/TriggerStrings.txt. On Windows reject known file lengths>=260 or directory lengths>=248 before native frontend start. Arbitrary archive members remain outside this bound.
implementation.externalRoot: SC2_NATIVE_WORK_ROOT captured for one retained bridge; ordinary absolute local directory disjoint from the map workspace and Toolkit installation. Relative, volume/share, overlapping and reparse-point roots are refused.
implementation.ownership: Full-entropy worker identity remains stable per bridge and distinct across bridges. Source maps remain workspace-contained. Saved output reads are bounded to this exact canonical worker; foreign/sibling output and digest mismatch reject before launch.
implementation.artifactPipeline: Copy native saved bytes into the suite, inspect, independently load/compile the exact digest and then launch. External output storage does not authorize arbitrary local inputs.
implementation.pathRejection: In-memory failed native job with reportPersistence memory_only; no report file or worker startup. Existing native handlers are not reset or redirected.

retainedParallel.scope: Four affected checks: directory cleanup ENOTEMPTY, two transport timeouts, journal rename EPERM. Do not attribute their cause solely to concurrency from a successful later run.

privacy.scope: Explicit private paths/debug/test artifacts and exact external C++/Python/Galaxy source copies, including renamed files. Not proof against transformed snippets or binary reverse engineering.

motivation.scope: The old handler remains live with one temporary component and no saved archive. Its expected localized paths exceed legacy Windows limits; this remains a path hypothesis, not a terminal diagnosis. A new controlled short-root native/game comparison is tracked separately.

openCoverage: Successful native save/reopen and exact saved-artifact game execution require their own finished result, independent of path-budget checks.
Arbitrary asset/member paths, broader topology/navigation/buildability, GUI/Data presentation and finished location art/gameplay remain separate.
Private-source exclusion does not guarantee protection against binary reverse engineering or transformed snippets.
